_doc: The bot's command vocabulary — the single source for the dispatch table, the Telegram '/' menu, /help and the README's command tables. Bot-specific, so it lives here rather than in browser/js/config.

help: Stencil bot — edit images with the same core as the browser/desktop/CLI.
Set the working image by sending a photo, an image file, or just an image link.
Add a caption command to apply it at once, e.g. a photo captioned /crop … or /filter bw.
Send a video to grab a frame (caption /frame n to pick one); or a .json file with caption /apply.
Image commands:
/prompt <request> — ask the AI assistant to plan and apply edits (/p for short)
/chat [on|off|clear] — chat mode: keep talking to the assistant without typing /prompt (clear forgets the conversation)
/chat save [on|off] — store the conversation with the active server project and restore it on /fetch (off by default)
/blank [format] [w h] [color] — start a blank canvas, e.g. /blank b5 pink
/format [name | custom w h] — page format for /blank and the saved layout (bare = list)
/url <link> — load an http(s) image
/sourcesite <link> [count] [filter=…] [format=…] — scrape a page's media into the chat
/sourceupload <link> [index=0] [format=…] — scrape a page and load one image to edit
/frame [n] — grab frame n of the loaded video (needs ffmpeg)
/crop <spec> [album] — crop, e.g. x1=10% x2=90% y1=10% y2=90%
/rotate <n> — rotate n quarter-turns clockwise, e.g. /rotate -1
/filter <bw|sepia|invert|contour|none|color> — recolour / tint (a colour = duotone)
/undo · /redo — step back / forward one edit   /reset — clear all edits
/drop — discard the working image
/image — re-render and re-send the current result image
/layout <json | link> — apply a layout JSON (or upload the .json file)
/json — download the layout JSON
/project — download the whole project as a .stencil file (send one back to open it)
/status — show the working image, edits and connections
Drawing (annotate the image — coords are pixels or x%,y%):
/draw line x1,y1 x2,y2 … — a polyline
/draw rect x1,y1 x2,y2 — a rectangle (two corners)
/draw poly x1,y1 x2,y2 x3,y3 … — a closed polygon
/color <#hex|name>   /thickness <n>   /points <n>
/style <solid|dashed|dotted>   /fill <#hex|name|none>
/pen — show the current pen   /undoline   /clearlines
Server commands:
/connect <url> [token] — connect to a collaboration server
/disconnect [url] — forget a connection
/connections [admin|session] — list connected servers (filter by credential)
/projects [url] — list projects (as buttons)
/fetch <name|id> — load a project as the working image
/create [name] — save the result as a new project
/save — save back to the active project
/sync [on|off] — live mode: auto-upload edits + pull peers' changes
/link — a link that opens the active project in the desktop app
/project-name <text> — rename the working image (or the active project)
/project-color <#hex|name|clear> — set the project's accent colour
/project-description <text> — set the description (empty clears; saved on /create)
/expire <n unit | never> — set the project's expiry, e.g. /expire 3 days
/delete — remove the active project from the server (asks to confirm)
/help — this message   /cancel — never mind
The inline buttons mirror these commands.

rows.effect: Greeting / full command list + the main menu

**Ask the AI assistant** to plan and apply edits — e.g. `/prompt make it sepia and crop 10% off each side`, or `/prompt give me 3 variants: rotated, tinted red, contoured`. The reply's validated op-plan (see [`llm-contract.md`](../llm-contract/llm-contract.md)) executes through the **same** editing service as the slash commands, so `/undo` etc. work on AI edits; the working image rides along as the vision attachment (a photo captioned `/prompt …`, or `/prompt` sent as a reply to a photo, targets that photo). One updated result comes back with the edit menu; variants arrive as a media album. A spinning **◐ Working on your request…** notice goes up the moment the turn starts (a vision plan over a big image can take a minute) and is deleted when the reply — or the error — lands. A turn that never delivered — it failed (timeout, unreachable endpoint, a truncated reply) or you ended it with the notice's **⏹ Stop** button — comes back with a **🔄 Retry** button that re-runs the same request, so recovering costs one tap instead of retyping it on a phone; a *refusal* has no button, since re-sending it verbatim would only repeat it

**Pick which chat API the assistant uses** — bare, it lists the ones the operator configured (`STENCIL_LLM_PROFILES`, see [`.env.example`](.env.example)) with a button each and a ✅ on the current one; `/chatapi llama` selects by name. The choice is **per user** and lives in the session, so one person trying a local model never moves anyone else, and it survives restarts. It is a picker, not free text: provider, base URL, model and token all come from the operator's environment, never from a chat message — a bot that took a URL from a message would issue requests to whatever host that message named. With no profiles configured the bot has exactly one chat API and says so

**Chat mode** — keep talking to the assistant without retyping `/prompt`. While it is on, every plain message you send is handled exactly like `/prompt <that text>` (same op-plan execution, same edit menu, variants as a media album). Started by `/chat` (or the **💬 Chat with assistant** button on the main menu / the **💬 Chat** button on the edit menu), stopped by `/chat off` or the **🚪 Chat off** button that rides the confirmation. `/chat clear` (or the **🧹 Clear chat** button next to it) makes the assistant forget the conversation so far without leaving chat mode; `/drop` clears it too. Precedence is strict: slash commands are never swallowed, an in-progress free-text flow (Rename / Describe / custom expiry) answers first, and a bare image link still loads like `/url` — only what's left over goes to the assistant. The flag lives in the per-user session (`UserSession.ChatMode`), so it survives across messages and shows in `/status`. `/chat save on\|off` (or the **💾 Save chats** toggle on the chat menu) is the contract-§12 **chat persistence** opt-in (default off, `UserSession.SaveChats`): with it on, after each assistant turn the conversation (text only, displayed replies, ≤ 32 messages — never images) is uploaded to the active **server** project's `chat` file kind and restored (history reseeded, "Restored N…" noted) when that project is `/fetch`ed again; `/chat clear` then also deletes the server copy. The bot keeps no local chat store, so without an active server project nothing is written
Start a blank canvas: a named ISO format (e.g. `b5`) **or** pixel dims (default A4 @ 96 dpi, white)

Set the page format (A0–C10, case-insensitive, or custom cm dims) — the `/blank` default page (custom cm dims convert to pixels at 96 dpi, like the CLI console), written into the saved layout's `pageSize`; bare lists all 33 formats
Load an `http(s)` image
**Scrape a web page's media** into the chat: the CLI fetches the page, extracts + filters its ``/`

**Scrape a page and load ONE image to edit** — the chat analog of the console `/source-upload`. Isolates the still at 0-based `index` (image-category only: `img\|background\|poster`, video excluded) via a one-item scrape, adopts it as the **editable** working image (replacing the session, like `/url`), then renders + sends it with the edit menu. Bare integer = the index; `format=`/`min/max` filter the candidate stills. Replies `No image at index N` when nothing lives there. The link is SSRF-vetted like `/url`
Grab frame `n` of the loaded video (needs `ffmpeg` on `PATH`)
Rotate `n` quarter-turns clockwise (bare lists the variants: `1`, `2`, `-1`)
Black & white, sepia, invert, edge-detect contour, clear, or a duotone tint
Clear pending edits (keep image) · forget the image entirely — `/drop` is a full start-over, so it also clears the assistant's conversation
Apply a layout: inline JSON or an `http(s)` link to a layout `.json` (same validation as uploading the file; links are SSRF-vetted like `/url`)
Download the rendered result · download the layout JSON
Show the working image, pending edits, pen and active project

Manage server connections. The URL may be an **invite link** (`<url>#token=<tok>`) — its fragment supplies the token; a token argument still wins over it. Each connection remembers what its credential turned out to be (browser parity: an **admin** token can't list projects but mints session tokens, and is proven once a mint-then-validate round succeeds); `/connections` marks those `[admin]` and takes an optional `admin` / `session` filter — tokens themselves are never printed
List server projects as tappable buttons (tap to fetch)
Load a server project as the working image
Publish the current result as a **new** server project
Save the result + layout back to the active project (version-guarded)

**Outbound deep link** — the reverse of `/start`: an `https` link (also the 🔗 Link button on the `/status` and edit menus) that opens the active project in the **desktop app**. Chat apps only linkify `http(s)`, so it points at the browser app's `launch.html` bounce page, which forwards to `stencil://open?server=…&id=…&version=…`. Server projects only (a link carries a reference, not image bytes) and **no token rides it** — whoever follows it connects with their own credential. The bounce page comes from `STENCIL_BOT_BROWSER_URL`

Set the active project's expiry (version-guarded) — bare `/expire` (or the ⏳ Expiration button in `/status`) opens a duration picker: **1 day · 3 days · 1 week · Fortnight · 1 month · 3 months · Custom · Never**; **Custom** awaits a free-text span like `3 days`, `week 4`, `2 weeks`, `1 month`

Inbound deep link: t.me `?start=` payloads from the browser/desktop **"Open in… → Telegram"** button decode to (server, project id); the bot connects like a fresh client (token minted via `POST /auth/token`) and fetches the project into the chat. Failures reply with the manual `/connect` + `/fetch` recipe
